setup: The PDF split-and-merge application is opened on a workstation, with the user ready to load documents for editing.
action: The user opens a PDF file in the graphical interface and inspects the document handling workflow.
expected_observation: The application presents a free graphical PDF manipulation workflow and no action in the session changes the contents of the original input PDF file on disk.

setup: The user has opened a multi-page PDF document in the application and the file is visible in the document list or page view.
action: The user chooses a split operation and defines split points to divide the document into separate output files.
expected_observation: The application produces separate PDF outputs according to the selected split points and displays the resulting split documents as distinct items ready for saving or export.

setup: Two or more source PDFs, or selected sections from PDFs, are loaded into the graphical workflow.
action: The user selects the desired files or sections and starts a merge into a new PDF document.
expected_observation: The application creates a new combined PDF in the selected order and shows the merged result as a single output document without modifying the source files.

setup: A PDF document with multiple pages is open in the application and the page thumbnails are visible.
action: The user selects specific pages to extract into a new document and confirms the extraction.
expected_observation: The chosen pages are copied into a separate PDF extraction result, and the original document remains available unchanged in the workspace.

setup: A PDF page is visible in the editor or preview and its current orientation is known.
action: The user rotates the selected page one step to the left and then one step to the right.
expected_observation: The page preview updates by 90 degrees for each rotation action, reflecting left or right rotation in clear 90-degree increments.

setup: A multi-page PDF is loaded and the page order is shown in thumbnail or list form.
action: The user drags pages to a different position in the sequence and confirms the new arrangement.
expected_observation: The page order in the document preview changes to match the user's rearrangement and the new sequence is shown before any save action.

setup: Two PDF documents are loaded and the application is in a mode that allows combining content from both documents.
action: The user selects alternating pages from the two documents to build a combined output.
expected_observation: The resulting composition shows pages interleaved from the different documents in the chosen alternating pattern before saving.

setup: The user has opened one or more PDFs and is working in the graphical composition view.
action: The user selects a set of pages and sections from the loaded documents to create a new PDF composition.
expected_observation: The application displays a composed PDF preview that reflects the selected pages and sections as a new document candidate.

setup: The user has assembled a split or merged PDF result in the application but has not yet saved it.
action: The user opens the preview of the generated result.
expected_observation: The application shows the assembled or split result in a preview view so the user can inspect it before saving or exporting.

setup: A composition preview is open and a page rotation, page reorder, or item removal is clearly needed from the visual review.
action: The user applies a lightweight correction directly in the preview, such as rotating an obviously sideways page, moving a page to the correct position, or removing an unintended item.
expected_observation: The preview updates immediately to reflect the adjustment, and the corrected page sequence or item set remains visible without requiring the user to restart the workflow.

setup: The graphical workflow contains at least one added PDF file and its pages are available for arrangement.
action: The user adds another PDF, removes an unwanted file or page, and reorders files or pages in the workflow.
expected_observation: The workflow updates to show the added and removed items and the revised order of pages or whole files is displayed clearly.

setup: The user has prepared a new PDF composition from multiple pages or sections and is ready to review it.
action: The user opens the composition preview before saving.
expected_observation: The system displays the final page sequence page by page, allowing the user to inspect the document in the exact order it will be saved.

setup: A composition preview is visible with pages drawn from more than one source PDF.
action: The user inspects the preview pages and their source information.
expected_observation: Each page in the preview shows which source file it came from, making the origin of every page identifiable at a glance.

setup: The user has created a composition that includes selected pages and excludes others from the source documents.
action: The user reviews the preview of the proposed output document.
expected_observation: The preview indicates which pages are included in the output and which source pages or sections are left out.

setup: A preview of the assembled PDF is open and the user notices that the page order or item set needs correction before saving.
action: The user rearranges pages in the preview or removes an unneeded item directly from the preview view.
expected_observation: The preview reflects the updated arrangement or removal immediately, and the revised result is ready for final saving.

setup: A PDF document is open in the page preview/inspection view and at least one page thumbnail or page canvas is visible.
action: The user increases the zoom level on the currently inspected page using the preview zoom control.
expected_observation: The page is redrawn at a larger scale, making text and page details visibly bigger while remaining within the preview view.

setup: A multi-page PDF is open in inspection mode with page navigation controls available.
action: The user steps forward one page at a time using the next-page control, then steps backward one page at a time using the previous-page control.
expected_observation: The inspection view advances exactly one page per step, and the displayed page number updates accordingly without skipping pages.

setup: A PDF page is visible in the inspection workspace and the document supports page enlargement.
action: The user opens the current page in a larger inspection view.
expected_observation: A larger page view opens for closer inspection, showing the same page content with improved readability and a clear way to return to the prior preview.

setup: A PDF with multiple pages is loaded and the split tool is configured for range-based splitting.
action: The user defines one split after page 3 and a second output section covering pages 5 through 7, then requests the split configuration preview.
expected_observation: The split plan shows separate output files for the configured ranges, with one file ending after page 3 and another file containing pages 5 to 7 as selected.

setup: A split preview is displayed showing tentative page boundaries for an upcoming output set.
action: The user drags or adjusts a boundary marker in the preview to move the split point to a different page before generating output.
expected_observation: The preview updates to reflect the new boundary position, and the affected output ranges change accordingly before any files are created.

setup: A split operation has been configured with multiple output documents derived from a single source PDF.
action: The user opens the split results preview before exporting.
expected_observation: The system lists the output documents in the exact creation order, and each entry clearly shows its page range and included pages.

setup: Several page sections from one or more source PDFs are selected for a custom output assembly.
action: The user arranges the selected sections into a new sequence and previews the assembled output before export.
expected_observation: The preview shows the sections in the chosen order, matching the intended final document structure without reordering them automatically.

setup: Two source PDFs are loaded for interleaving, and the user selects an alternating pattern between them.
action: The user starts the interleaving operation using the chosen alternating page pattern.
expected_observation: The generated sequence alternates pages from the selected source documents according to the user-defined pattern.

setup: Two source documents are selected for interleaving, each containing pages in a known internal order.
action: The user previews the alternating sequence before export.
expected_observation: Pages from each source appear in their original document order within the interleaved result, with no reversal or internal reshuffling.

setup: An interleaving setup is prepared where one source document has fewer pages than the other, and the user selects the mode to continue with remaining pages after one source ends.
action: The user generates the interleaved output with the chosen stop-or-continue mode after exhaustion.
expected_observation: The alternating sequence continues until the shorter source runs out, then the remaining pages from the other source are handled according to the selected mode, with no unexpected stopping or page loss.

setup: An interleaving or assembly job includes a source document with a known missing page reference or unavailable page slot.
action: The user previews the combined output before export.
expected_observation: The output preserves the pages that are available and displays a visible gap or missing-page flag at the missing position instead of silently replacing it.

setup: A source document is available in an interleaving or assembly workflow that allows repetition settings.
action: The user explicitly marks one source to repeat more than once in the output pattern and previews the result.
expected_observation: The preview reflects the repeated source occurrences in the sequence exactly as configured, confirming the source is used multiple times.

setup: A previewed split, merge, or assembly plan contains pages that appear duplicated or mismatched in a way that could indicate an accidental configuration error.
action: The user opens the preview of the planned output without forcing auto-correction.
expected_observation: The system flags the suspicious mismatch or possible duplicate pages in the preview and does not automatically rewrite the page selection to hide the issue.

setup: Two source documents are selected for interleaving, but they have clearly incompatible page sizes or a booklet-like layout that would distort the combined document.
action: The user attempts to start an interleaving operation with the incompatible sources.
expected_observation: The system warns the user that the combination is likely to break the document and steers them away from the operation rather than proceeding as a normal interleave.

setup: Two source documents have a page-size mismatch that is risky but not an absolute blocker, and the workflow allows controlled interleaving with warnings.
action: The user chooses the option to proceed with the merge/interleave despite the warning and opens the strong preview.
expected_observation: The system allows the operation only in controlled mode, shows a prominent warning, and provides a detailed preview of the resulting pages before export.

setup: The user has loaded two or more source PDF documents into the split-and-merge workspace, and alternating pages are configured so the result will be built from pages taken in turn from each source.
action: The user opens the preview for the alternating-page assembly before saving the output PDF.
expected_observation: The preview displays the resulting page sequence in the exact alternating order, showing the source document and page number for each entry so the user can confirm the output before saving.

setup: A PDF assembly has been configured with selected page ranges, rotated pages, and at least one included and excluded section visible in the workspace.
action: The user opens the final output preview before saving the PDF.
expected_observation: The preview clearly shows the page order, included sections, and applied rotations, allowing the user to verify the composition matches the intended final document.

setup: A split preview is open for a source document, and one split boundary is known to be incorrect or one expected page is missing from the split result.
action: The user adjusts the split boundary and restores the omitted page directly within the split preview.
expected_observation: The preview updates immediately to reflect the corrected boundary and restored page, and the resulting split set matches the revised page grouping before export.

setup: A saved project is open and one of its source files is missing, moved, renamed, or replaced, causing the file reference in the assembly to be unresolved.
action: The user initiates relinking for the broken source item before exporting the project.
expected_observation: The system accepts a replacement source file and updates the item so the assembly can continue using the corrected source reference for export.

setup: A source item in the workspace is flagged as needing relink because its original file cannot be found at the stored location.
action: The user chooses the browse option to locate a new file for that source item.
expected_observation: A file selection dialog opens, allowing the user to browse the filesystem and choose a replacement file for the missing source.

setup: A project file was saved with multiple source documents, and when reopened one source file is broken while other source files remain valid.
action: The user reopens the saved project.
expected_observation: The unaffected parts of the assembly remain visible and usable, while the broken source is clearly identified as unavailable without preventing work on the valid parts.

setup: A relinked source file has changed so that its page count or page order no longer matches the original version used by the project.
action: The user opens the affected section and remaps pages, reorders them, or removes and re-adds the problematic section.
expected_observation: The workspace allows the affected section to be corrected, and the page sequence updates to reflect the remapped, reordered, removed, or re-added content.

setup: The workspace contains a page that has been repeated multiple times in the assembly as separate visible entries.
action: The user selects one repeated instance and edits it in the workspace.
expected_observation: Only the chosen instance changes, while the other repeated instances remain as separate editable entries with their own settings preserved.

setup: A page appears more than once in the workspace as repeated instances, and each repetition is displayed as a distinct entry.
action: The user changes the position, rotation, or inclusion state of only one repeated instance.
expected_observation: The selected repetition updates accordingly, and the other repeated copies keep their original position, rotation, and inclusion settings unchanged.

setup: The workspace contains at least one source item whose link is broken because the file is missing or inaccessible.
action: The user views the assembly workspace containing the broken source item.
expected_observation: The broken link is clearly marked in the workspace with an obvious visual indicator so the user can immediately identify the unresolved item.

setup: A previously added page or section exists in an assembly, and the original source file has since been moved, renamed, or replaced.
action: The user selects the affected item and attempts to replace or reselect its source.
expected_observation: The system retains enough source reference information to let the user locate and rebind the item to a valid file without recreating the assembly from scratch.

setup: The user has selected a page range in a PDF assembly and is configuring repetition for specific pages.
action: The user chooses exactly which pages should repeat and sets the number of repetitions for those pages.
expected_observation: Only the selected pages are duplicated, and the workspace shows the exact repeat count requested for each chosen page or range.

setup: A page or page range is visible in the workspace and can be rearranged before export.
action: The user visually duplicates the page or page range and then changes the order of the duplicated items in the workspace.
expected_observation: The duplicate appears as a separate workspace item, and the updated sequence is reflected in the arrangement shown before export.

setup: The user has completed a workspace configuration that includes source selections, page ranges, rotations, repetitions, and merge or split layout choices.
action: The user saves the current workspace as a reusable project file.
expected_observation: A project file is created that can be reopened later to restore the saved workspace configuration.

setup: A previously saved workspace file exists with layout details, file selections, page order, split or merge structure, page ranges, rotations, repetitions, merge settings, and other arrangement choices.
action: The user opens the saved workspace file for restoration.
expected_observation: The system restores the working context as completely as possible, including the saved layout, file selections, page order, split or merge structure, page ranges, rotations, repetitions, merge settings, and other layout choices.

setup: A saved workspace or project file exists and contains a document list plus output settings from a previous PDF split or merge session.
action: The user opens the saved workspace or project file from the application.
expected_observation: The project opens with the same document list and output settings restored exactly as they were when saved.

setup: A project file was saved with source documents referenced by file path, and at least one referenced source has since been moved, modified, or deleted outside the application.
action: The user reopens the saved project file.
expected_observation: The application detects the path mismatch or missing source, and the reopened project shows the affected reference as unavailable or changed rather than silently substituting a different file.

setup: A saved workflow contains at least one missing, changed, or unavailable source file or output setting, and the original project file is stored on disk.
action: The user opens the saved workflow in the application.
expected_observation: A clear warning explains which source or setting cannot be resolved, and the saved workflow file remains unchanged on disk.

setup: A saved project contains one or more source PDFs that are no longer available at the recorded locations.
action: The user opens the saved project.
expected_observation: The project loads with the broken sources visibly marked as broken, and each affected item is ready for the user to relink to a replacement file.

setup: The user has configured a split or merge job and has not yet chosen a final output destination.
action: The user starts saving the generated PDF output and enters a preferred folder and filename.
expected_observation: The system saves the output to the user-chosen location using the user-provided name.

setup: The user previously saved a PDF output to a specific folder in an earlier session.
action: The user initiates another save operation for a new output file.
expected_observation: The save dialog opens in the most recently used folder rather than the default startup folder.

setup: A batch job or repeated versioning workflow is configured to create multiple output files in a folder that already contains files with matching names.
action: The user runs the job to generate additional output files without manually renaming each one.
expected_observation: The system prevents accidental overwriting by prompting the user, automatically appending a unique number, or applying the configured naming pattern so each output is distinct.

setup: The user is splitting a PDF into multiple output files and has not entered a custom naming rule.
action: The user starts the split operation.
expected_observation: The generated filenames follow a sensible pattern based on the original file name and the split sequence, such as an incrementing suffix for each part.

setup: A split job is prepared with default output names already generated by the application.
action: The user edits one or more output filenames before starting the split operation.
expected_observation: The renamed outputs are accepted and the saved files use the user-entered names instead of the default names.

setup: The user has selected an input PDF and has not specified any output filename or destination naming rule.
action: The user runs a split, merge, or extract operation.
expected_observation: The application generates a safe default output name derived from the input file name and does not require the user to enter one manually.

setup: A profile is configured with a defined output folder, or no output folder has been set and the input file resides in a known directory.
action: The user runs the configured PDF operation without choosing a different output location.
expected_observation: The resulting file is saved in the profile-defined output folder when one exists; otherwise it is saved in the same folder as the input file.

setup: The user is preparing different PDF operations such as split, merge, and extract without custom output names.
action: The user runs each operation type.
expected_observation: Each default filename clearly reflects the operation type, so split, merge, and extracted outputs are distinguishable from one another.

setup: The application is installed on a machine where the graphical interface is unavailable or not being used.
action: The user starts a PDF split or merge task through the command line.
expected_observation: The operation runs successfully from the command line without requiring the graphical interface to open.

setup: The user has a command-line environment available and wants to run a PDF job with specific inputs, page ranges, ordering, naming rules, and overwrite handling.
action: The user launches the job using command-line parameters or a saved job profile that defines the inputs, output path, split or merge mode, selected pages or ranges, order, naming pattern, and overwrite behavior.
expected_observation: The system accepts the supplied parameters or profile settings and executes the job according to those command-line-defined options.

setup: A reusable profile exists with saved defaults for input, output, split or merge options, and naming behavior.
action: The user runs the job from the command line while supplying override parameters for one or more profile settings.
expected_observation: The runtime command-line overrides take precedence over the stored profile values for the specified settings, and the job executes using the overridden values.

setup: The user is preparing a command-line split or merge job that requires an input PDF and an output location.
action: The user starts the job without providing one of the required parameters, such as the input file, page range, or output path.
expected_observation: The command fails immediately and prints a clear error message identifying the missing required parameter, without starting any PDF processing.

setup: The user is configuring a command-line job where a default behavior is already defined, such as using the full document unless a page range is supplied.
action: The user supplies an explicit command-line value that conflicts with that default behavior, such as requesting both full-document processing and a page-range-only operation.
expected_observation: The system rejects the request with an error explaining the conflicting options and does not produce an output file.

setup: An automated script or scheduled job is prepared to run the same PDF split or merge operation repeatedly with the same inputs.
action: The script invokes the command multiple times using the same explicit arguments and job profile settings.
expected_observation: Each run behaves the same way, producing the same output selection and naming results, with no dependence on hidden prompts, interactive choices, or remembered state from prior runs.

setup: The command-line tool is installed on two different platforms, and a batch script or shell script depends on documented option names and argument order.
action: The script calls the tool using the standard option names in the documented order on both platforms.
expected_observation: The tool accepts the same options consistently across runs and platforms, and the script completes successfully without needing platform-specific changes to option names or ordering.

setup: The user has multiple local PDF files to combine or process, along with an explicit page range, an output path, and additional command-line options such as split or merge mode.
action: The user submits a command that includes several input files, one or more page ranges, a destination file path, and the relevant options in a single run.
expected_observation: The system processes the specified files and page ranges in the requested order, writes the result to the chosen output path, and applies the supplied options predictably without ambiguity.

setup: The user has a PDF file and an output directory whose names contain spaces, such as a folder under a personal documents path.
action: The user runs a command-line split or merge operation while enclosing the file and folder paths in quotes.
expected_observation: The command interprets each quoted path as a single argument, successfully opens the input file, and writes the output to the intended location with spaces preserved in the path.

setup: The same PDF split or merge command is prepared for execution from a standard shell or batch file on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
action: The user runs the command from each platform's normal scripting environment without platform-specific rewrites of the core command syntax.
expected_observation: The command runs successfully in each environment, allowing the PDF operation to complete from standard shells and batch files on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

setup: The application has been installed on a workstation using the normal installation method for the operating system.
action: The user opens a fresh terminal or command prompt and enters the PDF split or merge command without specifying a full installation path.
expected_observation: The command is found on the PATH and starts successfully from the terminal, confirming that the installed executable is available system-wide.

setup: The user's computer is disconnected from the internet, and the PDF documents to be split or merged are stored locally.
action: The user performs a split or merge operation on those local PDF files while remaining offline.
expected_observation: The operation completes successfully using only local resources, with no prompt to connect to a network and no failure caused by the lack of internet access.

setup: The system is running in an environment with no network connectivity and no access to external services.
action: The user starts a core PDF operation such as merging or splitting local documents.
expected_observation: The PDF operation completes normally without attempting any network connection, login, cloud lookup, or remote service dependency.

setup: The user is working with local PDF files that are not meant to leave the device, and network access is available but not needed.
action: The user runs a split or merge job on the local PDFs.
expected_observation: The files remain on the local machine, no upload or sharing prompt appears, and the operation completes without transferring the documents to any remote location.

setup: The system creates temporary working copies during a PDF split or merge job and the job has completed successfully.
action: The user finishes the operation and inspects the temporary working area used by the application.
expected_observation: Temporary copies are removed automatically after they are no longer needed, and no leftover temp files remain once the job has completed.

setup: The user has a source PDF and chooses a normal split or merge action that should produce a separate result file.
action: The user runs the command without selecting any special in-place editing mode.
expected_observation: The original source PDF remains unchanged, and the system writes the result only to a new output file or separate working copy.

setup: The user has opened a source PDF that is intended to be processed by the tool.
action: The user attempts to execute an operation that would overwrite the same source file as the output destination.
expected_observation: The system refuses to edit the source PDF in place, blocks the overwrite attempt, and requires a separate output file instead.

setup: An advanced direct-on-originals mode is available in the application, and the user is currently in the standard default mode.
action: The user runs a normal PDF split or merge job without explicitly enabling the advanced direct-edit mode.
expected_observation: The system processes the job without touching the original file in place, and the direct-on-originals behavior remains disabled unless the user explicitly opts in.

setup: The PDF Split and Merge application is downloaded as a local desktop installer on a Windows, macOS, or Linux computer with no special network services configured.
action: The user installs the application and launches it on each supported operating system.
expected_observation: The application opens successfully on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with the same core PDF split and merge workspace available on each platform.

setup: A user has a standard desktop computer with no server access, no cloud account, and normal permission to install local applications.
action: The user downloads the application package and runs the installer locally.
expected_observation: The application installs and launches as a local desktop program without requiring the user to create or sign in to a cloud account, connect to a server, or complete any web-based setup step.

setup: The user has access to the application's public project page or distribution package.
action: The user opens the project's source code repository or source distribution information from the application website or package documentation.
expected_observation: The source code is publicly available with a visible open-source license and repository access, allowing the user to inspect, download, or contribute according to the published license terms.

setup: The application is installed on a computer that is offline or connected only to the local network, and the user is preparing to process a PDF file.
action: The user starts a split or merge operation without signing in to any external service.
expected_observation: The operation proceeds locally within the application, and no cloud login, remote processing requirement, or external service dependency is requested or required to complete the PDF job.

setup: The user reviews the application's installation package, included third-party notices, or about/license documentation before using it in a commercial environment.
action: The user checks the list of bundled components and their licenses.
expected_observation: The documentation identifies bundled components and their licenses clearly, and no included component is presented with unknown licensing terms or with a restriction that blocks normal commercial use of the application.

setup: The application is installed and ready to process local PDF documents.
action: The user opens the privacy statement or content handling notice from the application and reads the description before running a PDF split or merge task.
expected_observation: The application displays a clear statement that PDF content is processed only as needed to perform the requested operation and is not inspected or shared for unrelated purposes.

setup: The user has started a long-running split, merge, or page extraction job involving a large PDF or many source files.
action: The user watches the operation screen while the job is running.
expected_observation: A visible progress indicator updates during the job so the user can see that processing is ongoing and can tell the application has not stalled.

setup: The user starts processing a PDF file that is normal in size and typically completes quickly under normal conditions.
action: The operation takes significantly longer than expected to progress.
expected_observation: The application shows a warning that the job is taking unusually long for a file of that size, indicating a potential delay or issue rather than silently continuing without explanation.

setup: The user initiates a PDF job with missing input, inaccessible source files, or another blocking condition that prevents completion.
action: The application attempts to start or continue the job and detects that it cannot proceed.
expected_observation: The application stops the job cleanly and displays a clear explanation of why it cannot continue, such as a missing file, invalid input, or insufficient access.

setup: The user starts a long-running PDF operation that processes multiple pages or multiple input files.
action: The user monitors the progress area while the job is running.
expected_observation: The interface shows a simple progress bar together with the current page number or current file name being processed.

setup: The user has a PDF split, merge, or extraction job actively running in the application.
action: The user clicks Cancel or stops the running job.
expected_observation: Most running jobs stop promptly, the application ceases processing the current task, and the user is informed that the operation was canceled.

setup: The application is writing a single merged or split output PDF to disk and the user decides to cancel during the write process.
action: The user cancels the job while the output file is still being written.
expected_observation: The application handles the cancellation safely so the final output is not left as a corrupted or partially written PDF, and any incomplete result is not presented as a valid finished file.

setup: The user has an open layout or has unsaved changes in the application, such as a prepared merge order or selected pages that have not yet been saved.
action: The user attempts to close the application, close the current layout, or discard the current work.
expected_observation: The application shows a clear confirmation prompt warning that unsaved changes or open layouts will be lost if the user proceeds.

setup: The application has multiple layouts open at the same time, and at least one layout contains unsaved changes while another does not.
action: The user chooses to close the application or switch away from the open layouts.
expected_observation: The application handles each open layout separately in the confirmation flow, identifying which layouts contain unsaved changes and prompting for them individually instead of treating all layouts as one combined state.

setup: Multiple layouts are open, and the user has made changes in some layouts but not others.
action: The user chooses to save one or more modified layouts and discard only selected other layouts when closing or changing context.
expected_observation: The application allows the user to keep the chosen layouts by saving them, discard only the selected layouts, and leave the remaining open layouts unchanged.

setup: A saved PDF Split and Merge workflow is opened in the desktop app, and one of its referenced options has been removed or renamed since the workflow was last saved.
action: The user opens the saved workflow file.
expected_observation: The application displays which workflow settings are affected, highlighting the missing or changed option names and marking the impacted split or merge steps as needing attention.

setup: A saved workflow opens with one option value no longer valid for the current version of the application, such as an unavailable output mode or unsupported page range rule.
action: The user loads the workflow without manually correcting the invalid setting first.
expected_observation: The application applies a sensible fallback default where possible or leaves the invalid setting disabled, and the affected control is shown as requiring user correction before the workflow can be run.

setup: A saved project contains multiple configured split and merge steps, but one referenced source PDF file cannot currently be recovered or opened.
action: The user reopens the project file in the application.
expected_observation: The project still opens with all remaining saved settings preserved, the missing source file is flagged as unavailable, and no unrelated workflow configuration is lost.

setup: The user is preparing to save a workspace that includes split rules, merge order, and output naming preferences.
action: The user saves the workspace using the supported project/profile save option.
expected_observation: The workspace is stored as a simple project or profile file rather than a packaged archive, and the resulting file can be reopened as a standalone workspace definition.

setup: A saved workspace file references input PDFs and output locations by file path, and the user has enabled optional existence checking.
action: The user opens the workspace file and triggers path validation.
expected_observation: The application loads the referenced paths, reports which files still exist and which are missing, and keeps the workspace usable even when some paths no longer resolve.

setup: The user is running a command-line merge job that would normally refuse to overwrite an existing output PDF file.
action: The user supplies an explicit command-line override to allow overwriting the destination file.
expected_observation: The job proceeds with overwriting allowed according to the override, and the command-line response reflects that the overwrite behavior was taken from the user's explicit option.

setup: The user launches a split or merge job with explicit values for page selection and output behavior, while application defaults are also available for the same settings.
action: The user starts the job with both defaults and explicit values present.
expected_observation: The explicit user-provided values are used instead of the defaults, except where the combination would be invalid, in which case the job is rejected or adjusted with a clear validation message.

setup: An automated recurring job is configured with a job profile and a fixed set of input files and settings.
action: The same job profile is executed twice with the same inputs and settings.
expected_observation: Both runs generate the same predictable default naming pattern for the output files, and if a different job profile is used, its naming convention can differ while remaining consistent for repeated runs with identical inputs.

setup: The user is working from a terminal on a local machine and has a PDF split or merge task ready to be defined from command-line options.
action: The user enters split and merge parameters using command-line arguments instead of the graphical interface.
expected_observation: The application accepts the script-friendly parameters, parses the requested split or merge options correctly, and starts the job without requiring interactive GUI input.

setup: The PDF Split and Merge tool is installed on the user's desktop machine and available for both interactive use and batch execution.
action: The user runs the tool once through the desktop application and once as part of a local batch or script job.
expected_observation: The tool operates successfully in both standalone desktop mode and local script/batch mode on the user's own machine without requiring a remote service.

setup: The user opens an original source PDF and sets up a split or merge operation that produces a new output file.
action: The user runs the operation using the original PDF as input.
expected_observation: The original PDF file remains unchanged on disk, the application creates or updates only separate output files, and no in-place modification of the source document occurs by default.

setup: The user processes one or more PDFs on a local desktop machine with network access available.
action: The user starts a split or merge job from the application or command line.
expected_observation: The documents are processed locally on the machine, and no file contents are uploaded to any remote service during the operation.

setup: A job requires temporary working data such as extracted pages or intermediate merge artifacts to complete successfully.
action: The job runs to completion and the final output is produced.
expected_observation: The temporary data is retained only for the duration needed to complete the operation and is removed or released after the job finishes, unless it is still required for an active workflow.

setup: The user attempts to open a PDF that is either password-protected or unreadable due to file corruption or access restrictions.
action: The user starts processing the protected or unreadable PDF.
expected_observation: The tool does not fail silently; it shows an explicit warning or error explaining that the file is protected or unreadable and indicates whether any partial inspection was possible.

setup: The command-line tool is invoked with a PDF set that includes at least one seriously unreadable file and one protected file that can still be partially inspected.
action: The user runs the default command-line processing behavior on the file set.
expected_observation: The tool stops on the serious read error, emits a warning for the protected file when partial inspection is possible, and does not continue as if the unreadable file had been processed successfully.

setup: The user starts a command-line split or merge job, or reopens a saved job profile, where the profile includes a default page range or output behavior that conflicts with an explicitly entered value.
action: The user runs the job with an explicit command-line option or profile setting that overrides the default, such as a user-specified output path or page range.
expected_observation: The application uses the explicit user value instead of the default, unless the combination is invalid; if the explicit choice creates an invalid combination, the run is rejected with a clear error message rather than silently applying the default.

setup: The user has started a split or merge operation with missing input, an inaccessible file, or another blocking condition that prevents processing.
action: The user launches the operation with the unusable input or broken configuration.
expected_observation: The tool stops without continuing partial processing, exits cleanly, and displays a clear explanation of why it cannot proceed.

setup: The user prepares an interleave operation using source documents that clearly do not match in a way that would produce a broken result, such as incompatible page counts or an obvious ordering mismatch for the intended document structure.
action: The user attempts to interleave the mismatched sources into one output document.
expected_observation: The system does not perform the interleave operation and instead prevents creation of a clearly broken document, showing a message that the source mismatch makes interleaving unsafe or invalid.

setup: The user opens an interleaving workflow where one source document is needed more than once to achieve the intended output order.
action: The user explicitly adds the same source document multiple times in the interleave sequence.
expected_observation: The repeated source is accepted only because it was explicitly chosen, and the resulting output follows the user-defined repetition order without the system blocking it or changing it automatically.

setup: The user configures a merge or interleave job with intentional duplicate source entries to preserve a specific content order, such as repeating the same section or chapter in the final document.
action: The user saves and runs the job with the duplicate entries included exactly as arranged.
expected_observation: The saved job and produced output preserve the repeats exactly as configured, with no automatic collapsing, deduplication, or reordering that would change the intended content or sequence.

setup: The system is being packaged or prepared for distribution with optional third-party components whose license terms are unclear, non-commercial, or dependent on cloud services.
action: The packaging process includes one of these problematic components as a bundled dependency.
expected_observation: The component is excluded from the bundle, or the packaging is blocked with an explanation that unclear licensing, non-commercial restrictions, or cloud-service dependencies are not permitted in the distributed package.

setup: The application is preparing its dependency set or distribution bundle and has both permissive and more restrictive implementation options available for the same function.
action: The packaging or dependency selection process is executed for release.
expected_observation: The system selects the clearly permissive dependency or packaging approach where possible, avoiding choices that would add unnecessary legal burden to users.

setup: The command-line tool is available to the user with several PDF files in a working directory and valid page ranges available for selection.
action: The user runs the tool with multiple input files, explicit page ranges, an output path, and relevant options in a single command.
expected_observation: The command-line interface accepts the full set of inputs, processes the specified page ranges and options, and writes the output to the requested path.

setup: The application is installed on the system in a standard location without requiring the user to navigate to the installation folder.
action: The user opens a terminal and invokes the command by its name from any directory.
expected_observation: The tool starts successfully from the PATH without needing a full executable path, confirming it is available as a command-line program.

setup: The tool is installed on Windows, macOS, and Linux systems, each with platform-appropriate file paths and shell quoting conventions.
action: The user runs equivalent split or merge commands on each platform using paths that include spaces and shell-sensitive characters.
expected_observation: The command-line behavior is consistent across the three platforms, and each platform correctly handles its own quoting and path syntax without misreading file names or options.

setup: The user has an active workspace containing a list of source documents, page operations, output settings, and composition or layout choices.
action: The user saves the workspace and later reloads the saved file.
expected_observation: The reloaded workspace restores the same document list, page operations, output settings, and layout or composition choices that were present when it was saved.

setup: The user has saved a project that references source PDFs by file path, and at least one referenced file has been moved, renamed, or deleted after the project was saved.
action: The user opens the saved project.
expected_observation: The project loads the stored file paths and indicates which referenced files are still valid or missing, allowing validation of whether the paths still resolve to existing files.

setup: The user has replaced a source PDF with a newer file and relinked the project to the replacement while keeping the original reference history available.
action: The user opens the preview for the relinked source file.
expected_observation: The preview offers a side-by-side or thumbnail comparison of the relinked file versus the prior source, helping the user verify the replacement visually.

setup: The user has a normal-sized PDF file and performs a typical split or merge job with standard settings on a reasonably current workstation.
action: The user starts the split or merge operation and waits for completion.
expected_observation: The job completes near-instantly or within a few seconds, and it does not generally remain running long enough to be considered unusually slow beyond roughly ten to fifteen seconds.

setup: The user starts a longer-running split or merge operation with a large document or a more complex set of inputs.
action: The user initiates the operation and watches the interface during processing.
expected_observation: The system displays visible progress feedback, such as a progress bar, percentage, or activity indicator, so the user can tell the task is still running and has not stalled.

setup: The user opens the PDF Split and Merge application and loads a combined document containing many pages, including several high-resolution scanned pages and a mix of text and image content.
action: The user previews the document and runs a split or merge operation on the large combined file.
expected_observation: The application completes the operation without freezing or crashing, and the resulting output is produced successfully with all expected pages included.

setup: The user has loaded a PDF containing pages with different rotations, margins, alignment, and some pages intended to be included or omitted from the final output.
action: The user opens the preview and inspects the page sequence, page orientation, visible margins, and text clarity before confirming the job.
expected_observation: The preview clearly shows page order, rotation, omitted or included pages, and visible layout details well enough for the user to confirm the assembly visually.

setup: The user loads a scanned document with fine text, form fields, and layout-sensitive content such as signatures and boxes.
action: The user zooms into the preview and inspects the pages before saving or exporting the PDF.
expected_observation: The preview is rendered at sufficient resolution for the user to read scanned text, inspect form structure, and verify layout details without obvious blurring or pixelation that prevents review.

setup: The user has assembled a split/merge job with multiple source PDFs and selected an output name and destination folder.
action: The user reviews the final page order and output settings in the pre-save preview before clicking Save.
expected_observation: The application presents the assembled document clearly enough for the user to verify page sequence and selection before saving, reducing the need to redo the job after export.

setup: An automated or repetitive batch workflow is prepared with the same set of split and merge parameters used across multiple runs.
action: The workflow is executed repeatedly with the same inputs and settings across successive runs.
expected_observation: Each run produces consistent output naming, page selection, and operation behavior, with no unexpected changes in prompts, ordering, or results between runs.

setup: The user has selected a source PDF and configured an export path that could overlap with an existing output file name.
action: The user attempts to save the generated PDF using a name that matches an existing file or the original source document.
expected_observation: The application prevents accidental replacement by warning the user or requiring an explicit confirmation before overwriting, and no file is replaced without clear user consent.

setup: The user has an unsaved split or merge layout with page selections and ordering changes that have not yet been exported.
action: The user attempts to close the application, load a different document, or start a new job without saving the current layout.
expected_observation: The application prompts the user to confirm discarding unsaved changes and preserves the current layout if the user chooses to cancel the action.

setup: A saved workflow or command-line configuration is reused on different supported platforms and across multiple runs.
action: The user reopens or replays the workflow and compares the available option names and their ordering with the previous run.
expected_observation: The same option names appear consistently in the same logical order, allowing scripts and saved workflows to remain stable across executions and platforms.

setup: The user starts a long-running split or merge operation involving many pages or several output files.
action: The operation is executed while the user watches the progress display.
expected_observation: A clear progress indicator is shown that identifies the current page or file and displays completed progress out of the total, such as pages processed or outputs completed.

setup: The user is processing a password-protected or unreadable PDF and has selected the configuration that allows protected files to be skipped or reported as unprocessable.
action: The user runs the split or merge job including the protected or unreadable PDF.
expected_observation: The system skips the file or reports it as unprocessable according to the selected choice or command-line configuration, while continuing with other eligible documents where applicable.

setup: The user launches the command-line workflow with one or more required inputs intentionally omitted, such as a missing source file or required output specification.
action: The user submits the command without the required parameter.
expected_observation: The system stops immediately, reports the missing required input, and does not begin processing or create any output file.

setup: The user prepares a command-line request containing malformed arguments or file paths that do not exist.
action: The user submits the invalid command with the malformed or missing file references.
expected_observation: The system rejects the command, reports the invalid argument or missing file path, and does not proceed with the split or merge operation.

setup: The user starts a split or merge job on a normal-sized PDF that is taking unusually long to process due to unexpected conditions.
action: The operation continues beyond the normal time expected for that document size.
expected_observation: The system warns the user that the job is taking longer than expected instead of remaining silent, while continuing to indicate that processing is still active or needs attention.

setup: The system is writing a single output PDF and the user initiates a cancellation during the write process.
action: The user cancels the operation while the output file is actively being written.
expected_observation: The application handles the interruption safely, avoids leaving a corrupted final PDF, and reports that the output was not completed or was left in a safe state.

setup: A previously saved workflow is opened and one of its stored options now refers to a removed or changed output setting.
action: The user loads the workflow that contains the outdated setting.
expected_observation: The application preserves the rest of the workflow, marks the changed option as disabled or defaulted, and prompts the user to correct the affected setting before saving or running the job.

setup: The user has opened a merge or interleaving workflow with two source PDFs selected in the project. One document is a standard portrait A4 report and the other is a landscape booklet-style PDF with pages arranged as spreads, making direct interleaving unsuitable.
action: The user attempts to proceed with the normal interleaving or alternating merge operation.
expected_observation: The system blocks the normal interleaving workflow and presents a clear message that the selected documents are incompatible for interleaving because of differing page sizes or booklet-like structure, then steers the user toward an alternative workflow such as a different merge method.

setup: A saved project is opened that references a source PDF file previously added to the project. The original file has been moved, deleted, renamed, or is no longer readable at its saved location.
action: The user opens the project and attempts to prepare or run export.
expected_observation: The system marks the missing or unreadable source entry as broken in the project, shows that export cannot proceed with that source unresolved, and provides a relink action so the user can select a replacement file before exporting.

setup: A saved project contains a source PDF that has since been replaced with a newer version at the same path or relinked location. The new file has a different number of pages or a changed page order compared with the version originally used in the project.
action: The user opens the project or initiates export validation.
expected_observation: The system warns that the source file content has changed, specifically indicating that page count and/or page order no longer matches the saved project state, and it allows the user to review and adjust the selected pages before export continues.

setup: The user has selected one or more source files for a split or merge operation, and at least one of the files is malformed, encrypted without permission, corrupted, or otherwise cannot be parsed by the document processor.
action: The user starts processing the job.
expected_observation: The system stops processing and displays an error that identifies the exact file that failed, together with the reason it could not be processed, such as unreadable content, unsupported encryption, or file corruption.

setup: The command-line workflow scope is being reviewed before final release scope is confirmed.
action: A stakeholder asks which primary user group the command-line workflow is intended for.
expected_observation: The system requirements do not assert a final primary user group for the command-line workflow; the scope remains open and no acceptance scenario should assume a specific audience as finalized.

setup: The product team is considering support patterns for users who repeatedly edit and reprocess document sets over time.
action: A stakeholder requests a quantified expectation for how often recurring editing sessions will occur.
expected_observation: The requirements do not define an exact usage frequency for recurring editing sessions; the value remains unspecified and should not be treated as a confirmed workload assumption.

setup: A document rotation feature is being evaluated for the first release.
action: The user attempts to apply a rotation angle that is not a multiple of 90 degrees, such as 45 degrees.
expected_observation: Only fixed 90-degree rotation support is confirmed at this stage, so arbitrary-angle rotation is not an accepted requirement and should not be assumed available in the current scope.

setup: The core document-processing workflow is being defined without confirmed decisions about optional update checks or built-in help resources.
action: A user looks for update-check prompts or integrated help as part of the main processing flow.
expected_observation: No acceptance claim can be made for update checks or help resources in the core workflow, because these capabilities are not yet specified as part of the release scope.

setup: The open-source distribution license is under review and has not been finalized.
action: A release stakeholder asks which license will govern distribution of the tool.
expected_observation: The exact license choice remains undecided, so no finalized acceptance scenario should assert a specific open-source license as selected.

setup: The minimum viable release scope is being discussed, with competing options between a polished command-line experience and a lighter initial version.
action: A stakeholder asks whether the first release must include a fully polished command-line scope.
expected_observation: The requirement remains open, and the release definition does not yet confirm whether the minimum viable version includes a fully polished command-line scope or a lighter first version.
